note.question: How can threshold-based allocation policies support inventory management of red blood cells?
note.overview: Under current regulations, red blood cell (RBC) units can be transfused to patients up to 42 days after donation. However, recent studies suggest an association between the age of transfused RBCs and adverse clinical outcomes for their recipients. Therefore, there is an interest in inventory management policies that could reduce the age of transfused RBCs without compromising their availability.

Our approach is based on analyzing a sequence of modified Stage 2 inventory systems in which each unit can be allocated only during a finite number of Stage 1 idle periods, after its arrival at Stage 2.

From Kaspi and Perry (1983) we know that the outdate and loss processes of Stage 1, and therefore the supply and demand processes of Stage 2, are (delayed) renewal processes (with rates λq1 and μl1, respectively, as discussed previously).
